task_instance: Given a sample Node package repo whose GitHub Actions release workflow publishes with a stored NPM_TOKEN (NODE_AUTH_TOKEN) and whose package.json lacks a repository field, apply the skill's checklist to migrate the workflow to npm trusted publishing (OIDC): grant id-token write permission, set the npm registry on setup-node, ensure npm 11.5.1+, remove every publish token, add a matching repository.url, and strip the auth directive from .npmrc.
evidence: Created sample-repo (package.json, .github/workflows/release.yml, .npmrc) representing the broken pre-migration state: release.yml had no permissions block and published with NODE_AUTH_TOKEN from an NPM_TOKEN secret; package.json had no repository field; .npmrc carried an _authToken directive. Applied the skill's checklist by editing the files: added permissions {contents: read, id-token: write}; set setup-node node-version 24 and registry-url to the public npm registry; added an 'npm install -g npm@^11.5.1' step; removed the NODE_AUTH_TOKEN env from the publish step; added package.json repository {type:git, url: a github.com repo}; removed the auth directive from .npmrc. Wrote verify.py (PyYAML 6.0.3 + json) asserting each checklist/security item and ran 'python3 verify.py'. First run FAILED one check (a stray _authToken substring in an .npmrc comment), which I fixed; re-run reported all nine checks PASS (exit 0): id-token:write present, non-id-token scope kept, npm>=11.5.1 ensured via node24+upgrade, no token in publish/job/workflow env, no _authToken/npmAuthToken in .npmrc, registry-url present, repository.url names a github repo, github-hosted ubuntu runner, and the trigger (push tags) is not an untrusted event. Files: sample-repo/.github/workflows/release.yml, sample-repo/package.json, sample-repo/.npmrc, verify.py. The npm-side steps (registering the trusted publisher, deleting/revoking the old token) need the user's authenticated npm login with 2FA and network, which the skill's own Limitations explicitly hand to the user and are outside this offline repo-editing deliverable; the optional 'go-tokenless' npx automation was not used because it would require network package fetch, but the checklist was applied by hand instead.
